newsitem.title: USA: Boston's $700 mln convention center deal reached.
newsitem.headline: Boston's $700 mln convention center deal reached.

text.p: The Massachusetts House of Representatives will resume debate on a $700 million convention center for Boston on Tuesday, but the city's mayor and House speaker announced they had reached a deal Monday.
Under the accord's terms, Boston's share of the project to be financed by bonds will come to $157 million, some $27 million more than Mayor Thomas Menino said the city could afford.
"I think we got a compromise," Menino told reporters at a State House press conference. "I always said we could work this compromise out... we both wanted a convention center."

Meanwhile, Speaker Thomas Finneran, D-Boston, said, "Reasonable people can have differences of opinion. The mayor mayor and I have reached agreement on a number of issues" concerning the convention center and its funding.

A Republican amendment to put before the voters the hotel/motel tax in Boston, Cambridge, Worcester and Springfield that would help fund the state's share of the convention center went down to defeat on Monday 120 to 30.
Republican Gov. William Weld has threatened to veto the convention center measure if it fails to give voters a chance to approve the necessary tax hikes.
